title: dispatch.sh: route codex sessions across the two accounts (per-account caps, recorded in sessions.jsonl)

labels.name: infrastructure
labels.description: Foundational definitions, shared APIs, or supporting layers

body:
Two codex accounts are configured on ghz, each with a concurrency limit of 10: the primary home `~/.codex` and a second home `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/codex-home-yxy` (its `auth.json` and `config.toml` link to the owner's `auth-yxy.json` and `config-yxy.toml`; endpoint api.finite-dimensional.space; serves gpt-6-astra). Since 2026-09-05 17:20Z an interim PATH shim (`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/codex` v2, source `/tmp/codex-shim-v2`) routes `codex exec` sessions to the less loaded account by scanning `/proc` for live sessions and logs decisions to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/account-router.log`. Owner decision (2026-09-05, "both"): move the routing into the dispatcher so it is deterministic, capped per account and recorded in telemetry, then retire the shim's routing part.

Task (keep it small, about 150 workflow-layer lines):

1. `local/bin/dispatch.sh` gains `--account auto|primary|second` (environment `MIPSTARRE_CODEX_ACCOUNT`, default `auto`). `auto` picks the account with the smaller ratio live/cap; ties go to primary. Live counts are marker files `$CACHE_ROOT/accounts/<account>/<pid>` written before `codex exec` starts and removed when it exits (trap), with stale-pid cleanup on every read. Caps come from `$CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/max-codex-primary` (default 9) and `max-codex-second` (default 10); when both accounts are full, poll every 20 s up to `MIPSTARRE_ACCOUNT_WAIT` (default 1800 s), then proceed on the less loaded one.
2. The second account is selected by exporting `CODEX_HOME=${MIPSTARRE_CODEX_HOME_SECOND:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev/codex-home-yxy}` for that `codex exec` only (proven to work from worktrees: probe 2026-09-05 16:27Z). `primary` leaves `CODEX_HOME` unset.
3. Every `sessions.jsonl` row gains `"account": "primary"|"second"` and `"model": "<model id>"` (closes #231; `results/telemetry/model-comparison/compare.py` may then read the field directly and fall back to the rollout path for older rows).
4. `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` need no change beyond passing the environment through; document the variables in their headers.
5. Unit tests in `scripts/tests/test_dispatch.py`: the chooser as a pure function of (live counts, caps), stale-marker cleanup, and the `--account` argument validation. Keep `test_future_astra_mathfix_selects_model_effort_and_persona` green.
6. Protocol: one paragraph in `local/protocols/sessions.md` and an `EVOLUTION.md` entry citing the events.md entries of 2026-09-05 (two accounts, router shim) per `local/protocols/meta.md`.
7. PR body must state the follow-up for the operator: after the merge, replace the shim by its v1 behaviour (multi-agent off only; `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/codex.v1-20260904`) and set `max-codex` back to the sum of the two caps.

Not in scope: changes to the codex configuration files, to `lane` scripts under /tmp, or to the merge daemon.

body:
<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-stage43-magic-square-rigidity -->
### Motivation

Discharge the external Magic Square self-testing boundary used by QPBT
soundness. The canonical project statement is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
matched by `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. The cited
external source is Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.

The cited external proof obtains this as a robust linear-constraint-system
self-test using its general solution-group/stability machinery. This repository
has no such general framework. Formalize only the finite-dimensional Magic
Square consequence needed here; do not introduce a project-wide LCS or
approximate-representation mechanism.

### Target

After the Magic Square foundation/split packet #75, prove only the existing
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_rigidity` in
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean`, preserving its complete public
signature verbatim:

- one universal `C : ℝ` with `1 ≤ C`, before `ε` and `S`;
- every `ε ≥ 0` and every `S : Strategy msGame` with `1 - ε ≤ S.value`;
- an `MsRigidityWitness S`;
- the Euclidean state bound;
- Alice and Bob measurement-distance bounds at zero-based variables 0/X and
  4/Z;
- both anticommutator-distance bounds;
- all seven bounds at scale `C * Real.sqrt ε`.

### Dependencies

- Base on merged #75.
- Base on #49 for the clean state-dependent distance/observable conversion and
  triangle API, especially `opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le`,
  `consistencyDefect_postprocess_le`, and `povm_to_obs` where applicable.
- Base on #64 for clean EPR normalization and the Pauli-projector/observable
  expansions used to identify `idealMagicBitProj`.
- Base on #68 for the binary Pauli involution and twisted-commutation laws.
- It is independent of the perfect-strategy packet, #69, the fixed-field-model
  work, and encoding/decoding. Once the split and these three dependencies
  land, rigidity and perfect strategy may run concurrently in disjoint files.

### Proof route

1. Expand the game value over the 36 directed constraint-variable incidences.
   Convert `1 - ε ≤ S.value` into rejection-mass bounds, then into the
   finitely many row/column consistency relations with explicit constants.
   Include bounds for wrong-form answers folded by `msBitOrZero`; they are not
   definitionally absent.
2. Reduce arbitrary finite POVMs to projective measurements without
   strengthening the theorem. Reuse or adapt the proved one-measurement and
   tensor-product Naimark machinery in
   `MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkFull.lean`, but prove the
   pure-vector/intertwining consequences actually needed here: value
   preservation, composition of the input-space embeddings with the eventual
   self-test isometries, and transfer of state-dependent effect bounds back to
   the original strategy.
3. For the dilated projective strategy, turn the six nearly satisfied parity
   constraints and same-cell agreement into approximate reflection relations.
   Isolate a proved, file-local projective Magic Square rigidity lemma;
   projectivity must be discharged by step 2, not exposed in
   `exists_ms_rigidity`.
4. Follow the finite Magic Square operator argument: extract approximate Pauli
   `X` and `Z` pairs for the two logical qubits, construct the local swap
   isometries, and obtain a normalized auxiliary vector. Keep all intermediate
   relation/error lemmas concrete and proved. Do not restate
   Coladangelo--Stark's general theorem as an axiom or assumed proposition.
5. Translate the cited theorem's ideal observables `I⊗Z` and `ZX⊗ZX` through
   the explicit local basis change to the project's `X⊗I` and `Z⊗I`. Use
   #64/#68 to identify the corresponding
   binary effects with `idealMagicBitProj`.
6. Convert the self-test's density/trace estimate to the exact Euclidean vector
   estimate. Account for the square-root loss explicitly; this is not a
   definitional `simpa`.
7. Derive the four `msOperatorDistanceA/B` bounds, then the two
   `msAnticommutatorDistanceA/B` bounds from binary observable expansion,
   multiplication stability, and the squared-distance triangle estimates from
   #49.
8. Track explicit constants throughout and take a finite maximum to obtain the
   single universal `C ≥ 1`. Handle the theorem's unrestricted `ε ≥ 0`: use
   the robust argument in its small-error range and a separately
   proved coarse large-error bound with canonical padded isometries. Do not
   silently assume `ε ≤ 1`.

Private implementation submodules under
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Rigidity/` are allowed when they keep
individual proofs reviewable. They remain owned by this one issue and must
bottom out in Lean/Mathlib and the already proved local APIs.

### Statement integrity

Paper assumptions: an arbitrary finite-dimensional strategy whose Magic Square
success is `1-ε`. Lean uses arbitrary finite local carriers, a unit pure state,
arbitrary POVMs, nonnegative `ε`, and a lower success bound; the
lower-bound form is the faithful monotone version of the source equality.
Paper conclusion: local isometries extracting two EPR pairs and an auxiliary
state, four binary measurement approximations, and Alice/Bob anticommutation,
all with universal `O(sqrt ε)` control. Lean records exactly these
through `MsRigidityWitness`, `idealMsState`, `msOperatorDistanceA/B`, and
`msAnticommutatorDistanceA/B`; indices 0 and 4 are the paper's variables 1 and
5. Verdict: faithful explicit-constant encoding.

The paper explains two translations at lines 650-652: trace norm to Euclidean
distance and a local basis change. Both are proof obligations. No additional
strategy-projectivity assumption, bridge package, residual input, or changed
error exponent is source-faithful.

### Ownership and non-goals

Own `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean` and, if needed, new private
rigidity-only submodules below
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Rigidity/`. Do not touch
`MagicSquare.lean`, `MagicSquareTheorems/Basic.lean`,
`MagicSquareTheorems/PerfectStrategy.lean`, Pauli/distance source files,
blueprint, re-exports, or downstream soundness files.

Do not add `S.IsProjective`, restrict the strategy dimension, drop either
player's conclusions, omit the wrong-form answer analysis, move `C` under
`ε` or `S`, replace `sqrt ε` by a weaker rate, add an
external-theorem axiom, leave a conditional self-test helper, or create a
general LCS/group-stability framework. Do not add new issues merely for
mechanisms discovered during proof work; keep necessary private lemmas in this
packet.

### Acceptance

- `exists_ms_rigidity` is complete with its exact existing signature and all
  seven bounds.
- Every helper on its proof path is kernel-checked; its `#print axioms` output
  contains no `sorryAx` or new axiom.
- The owned file/submodules contain no `sorry`, `admit`, prohibited bypass,
  conditional bridge, or `**Unfaithful:**` dependency.
- The statement-integrity audit explicitly records POVM generality, quantifier
  order, zero-based indices, the universal constant, trace-to-Euclidean
  conversion, local basis change, and the large-error branch.
- Focused rigidity modules and `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean` type-check; full build,
  declaration check, blueprint render/status checks, diff check, exact-head CI,
  and independent review pass.
- Existing blueprint declaration links remain unchanged; no new `\leanok` claim
  is added.

body:
## Open now (answer in a comment)

| id | question | reply with |
|---|---|---|
| — | none open (B5 resolved 2026-09-04 21:26Z: A′, with latitude for A″ if correct and sufficient) | |
| B6 | PR 197 infra budget override or split | resolved (ceiling 1000, exemption fixed) |

Older comments that were superseded or were automatic alerts are hidden as outdated so the thread stays short.

---

This issue is the single place where the operator session (qpbt-main) asks the owner for a decision. It stays open and pinned; nothing else uses the `needs-owner` label. The owner is a human who checks GitHub occasionally and wants to catch up in one minute; every comment here also reaches the owner by email.

## When to post here — the test

Post ONLY if all three hold:
1. the item cannot move at all without the owner (credentials; the scope budget `MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE`; a mathematical design choice that changes what is being proved or what the paper claims);
2. no protocol, persona rule, or standing briefing lets you decide it yourself — if one does, decide, record the reason in `results/telemetry/events.md`, and continue;
3. you have already parked the item and have other queue work to do meanwhile.

**Mathematical gaps are not owner blockers by default (owner rule, 2026-09-04 22:35Z; defaults confirmed 23:05Z).** When a source statement is found mathematically wrong, the operator does not open an item here. Instead: (1) dispatch a Fable 5.1 math-fix session (astra once available; if Fable's window is exhausted, Opus iterates and Fable checks the result before adoption) to produce a corrected statement that is *correct* (no counterexample; a proof sketch from the cited source theorem) and *sufficient* (supports every use in the paper and in the blueprint dependency graph, not only the consumer that exposed the gap), preferring the option closest to the source (smallest added hypothesis, no change to definitions or the game); (2) iterate between the mathematics and the Lean implementation: convergence means the corrected statement type-checks, the downstream consumers still compile, and the gap note carries the counterexample and the proof sketch — a machine-checked proof of the corrected theorem is the proving packet's job, not a convergence condition; (3) budget: at most 10 math-fix sessions per gap, or roughly 1.5 working days, then an item here with all attempts attached; escalate immediately only if the fix would change a paper definition or the game itself; (4) record every adopted correction as a paper-gap note plus blueprint fix, announce it in one line on #27 (corrected statement and note path) so the owner can veto, and log it in `results/telemetry/events.md` and `results/telemetry/design-decisions.md`.

If in doubt, decide it yourself and record it. A wrong self-decision is recoverable; an idle project is not. Reviewer findings, workflow ergonomics, tooling choices, and "which order" questions are never owner blockers.

## Format — plain and short (hard cap: 10 lines above the fold)

Write for a human who has not seen the project in days. No jargon, no SHAs, no file paths above the fold, no protocol section numbers. Question first.

```
### BLOCKER <id> — <plain title, ≤ 8 words>
<!-- owner-inbox id=<id> status=open -->
**What I need from you:** one question, with the options (A/B/…) and which one I recommend and why, in ≤ 3 sentences.
**Why only you can decide:** one sentence.
**What happens meanwhile:** one sentence (what I am working on instead; nothing is waiting idle).
<details><summary>Details, if you want them</summary>
Issue/PR numbers, heads, file paths, the full reasoning, alternatives considered.
</details>
```

`<id>` is `B` + a running number (B1, B2, …). One blocker per comment. Do not repeat a blocker; do not add commentary.

**Owner — to answer:** reply with a comment starting with `DECISION <id>:` in plain words (e.g. `DECISION B3: agree`, or `DECISION B3: option B, and also …`).

**Operator — closing the loop:** at the start of every loop iteration and at every stage boundary, read this issue's comments (`gh api repos/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/26/comments --paginate`), find `DECISION <id>` comments for ids still `status=open`, act, then post `RESOLVED <id>: <one line>` and edit the original BLOCKER comment's marker to `status=resolved`. A blocker with no decision stays parked; never re-ask.

**Everything else** (progress, stage reports, what merged / what is dispatched / what is next) goes to the pinned "Progress log" issue #27, not here.
